transcript.text: First, let's rule out a drainage problem because a washing machine won't spin while water is still in it. When it stops, is there water left standing in the drum (not just wet washing)?
no water left in the drum, its empty just the wet mat. it drained fine

Thanks for letting us know that the water drains away during the cycle. This helps narrow down what might be happening with your washing machine. During the wash part of the cycle, does the drum turn back and forth, or does it not turn at all?
yeah it turns back n forth, sloshes about. tries to speed up then slows down a few times then gives up

Thanks for letting me know about the drum jerking and failing to speed up. Please pause or cancel the programme and wait for the door to unlock on its own before opening it. Washing machines refuse to spin if the load is out of balance — a single heavy item such as a bath mat, rug, duvet or a pair of jeans on its own, or a very small load, is the usual trigger. Spreading the washing out evenly or adding a few smaller items usually lets it spin. Was it a single heavy item or a very small load, or a normal mixed load?
it was just the big heavy rubber backed bath mat on its own, washed it cos the dog got it dirty

Thanks for letting us know it only fails with heavy loads. It is also worth checking the settings: wool, delicate and hand-wash programmes spin very gently, and options such as "no spin", "rinse hold" or a low spin speed stop the final spin. Was a normal programme with a normal spin speed selected, or was one of those options set?
its on the normal 1000 spin, not no spin. i didnt change any settings

[Heading: Out-of-balance load]
Thank you for confirming those settings are normal. Based on what you have described, an out-of-balance load is the most likely cause, although I cannot confirm this with certainty from our current information. Please try running evenly spread, mixed loads to see if that helps. If the machine continues to refuse to spin with normal loads, an appliance engineer can check the balance sensing and suspension. I am not recommending a specific part at this stage.
